title: Ladder stitch
subtitle: Parallel straight stitches linked by crossed or straight threads to form a band
excerpt: Ladder stitch (embroidery band stitch) builds a wide rectangular band from pairs of straight stitches set across two parallel lines, then linked at regular intervals by horizontal bar threads. The result looks like a ladder laid flat on the fabric.
sourceNotes: Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886). Caulfeild and Saward, Dictionary of Needlework (1882), ladder stitch entry. Note: this is the decorative surface band stitch, not the slip-stitch seam-closing technique of the same name.

content.text: Ladder stitch works between two parallel lines. Straight stitches cross from one line to the other at regular intervals, forming the rungs. Each rung is worked in turn down the band, so the needle travels along the back between the two lines. The open spaces between rungs give the stitch its characteristic airy ladder appearance.

items.label: Thread
items.value: Stranded cotton, 3 strands, or a single strand of perle cotton no. 5

items.label: Fabric
items.value: Firm cotton or linen; the band stays flat on a tightly woven fabric

content.text: Mark two parallel lines the desired band width apart, typically 6 to 12 mm. Also mark the rung positions at even intervals along both lines.
Secure the thread at the top of the left line. Bring the needle up at A on the left line and insert at B on the right line, directly opposite. This is the first rung.
On the back, carry the needle along the underside of the right line and bring it up at C, the next rung position on the right line.
Insert the needle at D on the left line, directly opposite C. Carry along the back to E on the left line, the next rung position, and bring up at E.
Continue alternating: each rung travels straight across from one line to the other. The back travels down the outer edges, keeping the front clean. Work all rungs to the end of the band.
To finish, secure the thread by running it under two or three rungs on the back. Trim close.

items.symptom: The rungs are not straight across the band
items.cause: The opposite points on each line are not level with each other.
items.fix: Mark the rung positions on both lines together using a ruler and set square before starting.

items.cause: The stitches are pulled too tightly or the fabric is not held taut.
items.fix: Work with the fabric in a hoop and pull each rung stitch with consistent, moderate tension. The rungs should lie flat without indenting the fabric.

items.symptom: The rung spacing is uneven down the band
items.cause: The back travel between rungs varies in length.
items.fix: Pre-mark all rung positions on both lines before starting so the intervals are fixed.

content.text: Ladder stitch makes geometric borders, decorative bands on clothing, and grid foundations for composite stitches. For a band with crossing diagonals rather than straight rungs, try
